title: [MIG-002] Define the extraction inventory, public API and project configuration contract
objective: Agree the smallest complete reusable library boundary and compatibility contract before moving implementation.
inScope: Inventory all 24 source modules plus schemas, semantic contracts, CLI commands, tests/helpers, scripts, docs, task records, runtime assets and CI. Classify each as Vibez implementation, consumer-owned input, test/example, or historical archive; assign exact source/destination paths and owners.

Recommend one ESM TypeScript/Node package with deliberate supported exports for project composition, registry/lifecycle, validation/evidence/review, orchestration/provider, PR/merge and diagnostics/recovery. Publish a supported capability map, not every accidental internal path.

Define a versioned project configuration and injected service graph: canonical project/worktree identity, tasks/requirements/contracts, state/evidence/exchange roots, validators, branch/base/check policy, review roles, providers, credential references and budgets. Separate immutable packaged schemas from exact-revision project inputs. Define precedence and hash/currency rules; secrets never enter tracked config.
Agree seams with #78's reusable profile/driver and #75's application service/supervisor so neither invents another config or lifecycle engine.

Record decisions for final package identity, distribution/license rights, supported Node/Windows/POSIX/local-filesystem matrix, history strategy and rollback window. Default: allowlisted provenance snapshot, compatible ipt.* record IDs, immutable tarball/checksum first; do not presume npm publication or choose a license without owner rights.
Specify how library-owned semantic contracts are discoverable in downstream architecture context while project-owned requirements/contracts remain revision-bound.
**Expected surfaces:** Architecture decision records, migration path manifest, public interface/config/schema specifications, capability/support matrix, consumer example specifications.
outOfScope: No source export, provider implementation, HTTP server, arbitrary workflow designer or renaming of persisted schema identities.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-01: Every reusable and historical surface has an explicit ownership/destination decision, including reusable scripts/CI and consumer contract context.
AC-02: Documented API and configuration support the complete existing lifecycle and #75/#78 consumers without internal imports or duplicated configuration.
AC-03: Package assets, project content and mutable state have distinct resolution rules and project-scoped identities.
AC-04: API, CLI, schema, state and adapter compatibility policies are explicit; first extraction preserves ipt.* historical identities and meaning.
AC-05: Release-blocking identity/channel/license/support decisions have recorded owners and resolution criteria; public distribution cannot proceed while rights are unresolved.
AC-06: Source-delta capture, final synchronization checkpoint and end of duplicate code ownership are specified.
validationPlan:
Trace each #74 M-AC requirement and each current module/CLI capability to an inventory entry and downstream test owner. Review two example consumers with different roots, validators and overlapping task IDs. Architecture review evaluates semantic producer/consumer behavior, including #75/#78.

Use applicable repository build/test/schema/contract checks. Retain exact commands/results, package/source/config identities and an acceptance-to-evidence map. Existing or fake-provider fixtures are not independent live review or task-completion evidence. This task is normal feature work, not a new canary requirement.
npm run build; npm test; python schemas/validate_fixtures.py; python schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py; npm run test:adversarial:mutations. Add issue-specific checks before admission.
